brief.headline: Close the ₹16.09 L price gap by matching Mars Plastics on bottles and caps, or we move volume to Manjushree or Mold-Tek.

priceAsk.summary: Match Mars Plastics on the 30ML HDPE bottle (₹1.38/NOS) and the 28MM PP cap (₹0.81/NOS), and close the gap on the 60ML bottle to Cincorp's ₹2.20/NOS.
priceAsk.target: Cutting our price on the 30ML bottle from ₹1.65 to ₹1.38 alone saves us ₹11.74 L a year; the cap drop from ₹0.90 to ₹0.81 saves another ₹4.23 L. Total opportunity: ₹16.09 L.
priceAsk.basis: We already pay ₹1.38/NOS to Mars Plastics for the same 30ML bottle and ₹0.81/NOS for the same cap — Premier is 19.6% and 11.1% higher. Market asking prices for a 28MM induction-wad cap run ₹0.55–1.20/pc (typical ₹0.85–0.95), so our ₹0.90 is market-fair but Mars proves ₹0.81 is achievable. No reason to pay Premier more for identical items.

paymentTermAsk.summary: Move from 45 days after receipt to 30 days, then explore 15 days for an extra cut.
paymentTermAsk.cashImpact: Going to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L of our cash; a further move to 15 days frees another ₹5.31 L.

brief.financialLeverage: Premier Plastic publishes no financials, so we can't see their revenue, profit or how tight their cash is. That means we build our case purely on our own purchase data and the market. Our ₹1.29 Cr annual spend is real money to a private converter, and we have two strong, audited alternates ready — Manjushree (₹2569.83 Cr, health B 65/100) and Mold-Tek (₹1010.97 Cr, health B 73/100) — both of whom serve pharma and can handle bottles and closures at scale. Without visibility into Premier's finances, we lead with the price evidence and the credible threat of shifting volume, not a hard squeeze.

evidence.point: We pay Premier ₹1.65/NOS for the 30ML HDPE bottle but Mars Plastics charges us only ₹1.38/NOS for the same item.
We pay Premier ₹0.90/NOS for the 28MM PP cap but Mars charges ₹0.81/NOS.
Market asking prices for a 28MM induction-wad PP cap are ₹0.55–1.20/pc, typical ₹0.85–0.95, with headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume.
Total excess we pay Premier versus the best prices we already get elsewhere: ₹16.09 L per year.
Moving payment terms from 45 days to 30 days frees up ₹10.63 L of our cash.

alternates.name: Manjushree Technopack Ltd
alternates.why: India's largest rigid-plastic packaging converter (₹2569.83 Cr revenue, health B 65/100) — already serves pharma with bottles, caps and preforms; top second-source candidate.

alternates.name: Mold-Tek Packaging Ltd
alternates.why: Listed rigid-plastic leader (₹1010.97 Cr revenue, health B 73/100) specialising in pails, containers and pharma packaging — a robust, profitable alternate for bottles and closures.

risks: Premier has no public financials, so we can't gauge if a hard push on price and terms might tip them over — keep the tone firm but not punitive, and frame it as 'help us keep you in the mix.'
Mars Plastics already beats Premier on the two biggest SKUs; if Premier won't move, we risk looking like we didn't need this meeting — so be ready to shift volume fast if they stall.

The market asking price for the 28MM cap shows 'modest headroom to ₹0.65–0.80 at higher volume' — if we consolidate with one supplier we may unlock that lower band, making Premier's ₹0.90 even harder to defend.

Manjushree and Mold-Tek are both large, healthy and pharma-experienced, so Premier knows we have real options — but neither is yet qualified or priced for these exact SKUs, so don't bluff a signed backup deal we don't have.
brief.suggestedOpeningLine: We want to keep you as a supplier, but right now we're paying you ₹16 lakh more each year than we pay others for the same bottles and caps — let's talk about how we close that gap and make the commercial work for both of us.
